title: What Are India's Foreign Exchange Reserves and Why Are They Changing?
description: India's foreign exchange reserves are like a country's savings account in foreign currencies and gold. They recently fell to around $726 billion as of October.

faq.q: What is the current level of India's foreign exchange reserves?
faq.a: As of October 9, 2026, India's foreign exchange reserves stood at $726.027 billion.

faq.q: Why did India's forex reserves fall recently?
faq.a: The reserves fell primarily because the Reserve Bank of India sold US dollars to prevent the Indian Rupee from depreciating too much against the dollar, amidst pressures like rising crude oil prices and foreign investor outflows.

faq.q: Is this the lowest India's reserves have been?
faq.a: No, India's foreign exchange reserves had reached a record high of $785.706 billion on September 4, 2026, before the recent decline. The current level is still substantial.

faq.q: How often does the RBI update foreign exchange reserve figures?
faq.a: The Reserve Bank of India typically releases its weekly statistical supplement, which includes the foreign exchange reserve data, every Friday.

faq.q: Do other countries also hold foreign exchange reserves?
faq.a: Yes, most countries hold foreign exchange reserves to manage their currency, pay for imports, and maintain financial stability.
